sources.quote: Every change must either declare at least one capability (new or modified) or explicitly opt out of specs: `openspec validate` rejects a change with zero deltas unless the change's `.openspec.yaml` sets `skip_specs: true`.

items.downgrade_reason: The skip_specs opt-out cannot be expressed, so the check would wrongly fail changes that opt out legitimately.

items.note: Checking this means comparing the Modified Capabilities names with the existing openspec/specs/<path>/spec.md paths at BASE_SHA. The section is not a compiled label, and capability names and file paths are written differently, so no selector can line them up.

items.note: The rule says every openspec show call must include --type spec. That needs a negated, all-calls check, which neither the cli rule nor prohibited_action can express.

sources.quote: and keep `--type spec`: a change and a spec sharing a name is otherwise an ambiguous-item error.

unitemized.reason: Every listed capability, modified ones included, needing a delta spec is already checked by the schema-023 item (openspec.capabilities listed_have_specs). Whether a change is spec-level or just implementation detail is a judgment call.
Leaving Modified Capabilities empty depends on whether requirements change, which is a judgment the run cannot reveal. The section is also not a compiled template label.
